predecessors.name: Tughlaq dynasty
predecessors.text: Lakhnauti, taken by Ilyas Shah in 1342; Bengal had been a Delhi province since 1225 and split into Sonargaon, Gauda and Satgaon in 1325

predecessors.name: Sonargaon Sultanate
predecessors.text: Sonargaon, the Mubarak Shahi realm of Fakhruddin and Ikhtiyaruddin Ghazi Shah, taken in 1352

successors.name: Sur Empire
successors.text: Bengal west of the Teliagarhi pass from 1536-37 and the whole sultanate after Gaur fell on 6 April 1538

ledger.x: 1342: Ilyas Shah conquers Lakhnauti.

c. 1350: Tirhut occupied. 'He first occupied the Tirhut region, which he divided into two parts': 'The part north of the Budhi Gandaki River were restored to Raja Kameshwar Thakur of the Oiniwar dynasty' while 'Ilyas kept the southern part for himself, stretching from Begusarai to Nepal Terai', with headquarters at…
1352: Ilyas Shah takes Sonargaon and unifies Bengal.
1353: Firuz Shah Tughluq occupies Pandua.
1355: 'Firuz Shah returned to Delhi in 1355'; Ilyas 'regained control of Bengal' and pursued as far as Varanasi.
1359: 'Delhi again invaded Bengal' (second Ekdala); 'the Delhi forces were repulsed' and a treaty followed 'recognizing the independence' of Bengal.
1359: the treaty after the second Ekdala siege recognises Bengal's independence.
1390: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah's reign begins and Sonargaon becomes the capital (infobox 1390-1410).
1395: the Bihar block goes to Jaunpur in Cliopatria (the year the Jaunpur row starts); the Bengal page is silent.
1410: the capital returns to Pandua (infobox Pandua 1410-1433).
1414: Raja Ganesha's house replaces the Ilyas Shahis.
1415: the Bengal-Jaunpur War begins.
1420: 'Parts of Jaunpur were annexed' in the war of 1415-1420 (Bengal page; no place named).
1420: the Bengal-Jaunpur War ends.
1430: Arakan restored as a Bengali vassal.
1433: Gaur becomes the capital (infobox Gaur 1433-1565); the article gives Mahmud Shah's move from Pandua to Gaur as 1450.
1435: the Ilyas Shahis are restored (infobox 1435-1487; the article has 1433-1486).
1437: Arakan annexes Ramu.
1447: Kapilendra Deva's campaign.
1450: 'An inscription in the Jagannath temple of Puri that is dated to the year 1450 CE narrates the conquest of Gauda': the last dated mention of the campaign.
1459: Arakan beats Bengal and takes Chittagong.
1459: Arakan ceases to be a Bengali vassal with its victory over Barbak Shah.
1459: Jessore and Khulna join.
1464: Tripura becomes a vassal.
1482: the south-bank part of the Bihar block (Patna) is Bengal's in Cliopatria's 1482 step; no page dates it.
1487: the Habshi (Abyssinian) kings take the throne (infobox 1487-1494; the article has 1486-1493).
1492-1493: Shamsuddin Muzaffar Shah attacks Kamata.
1494: Alauddin Hussain Shah founds the Hussain Shahi dynasty.
1496: Sikandar Lodi invades Bengal.
1496: the Barh treaty fixes the Lodi frontier at Barh (a sharp line).
1496: the Barh treaty.
1499: Kamata annexed up to Hajo.
1499: the Kamata war ends with the annexation up to Hajo.
1508-1509: Ismail Ghazi's raid from Mandaran fort 'reached Puri, but Gajapati Prataparudra drove the Bengal army back'; border fighting continued.
1512: the second Arakan war begins ('the war of 1512-1516').
1513: part of Tripura annexed.
1515: Orissa a Bengal vassal.
1515: the Orissa border fighting ends in the vassalage of Orissa.
1516: Chittagong back.
1516: the Arakan war ends ('The hostilities probably ended in 1516').

c. 1523: Nasrat Shah annexes the lands up to the Tons river: 'annexed the lands up to Tons river soon after 1522', after 'the collapse of the Lodi authority in Bihar' and 'entering into an alliance with the Lohani rebels'; the page also has his Sar-i-Lashkar build a mosque in Sikandarpur, Azamgarh district, in 1527.…
1526: Mithila annexed.
1532: Turbak invades the Ahom kingdom 'with a force comprising 1,000 cavalry, 30 elephants' and guns.
October 1532: Min Bin takes Chittagong.
11 December 1532: 'Arakanese forces entered Dhaka on 11 December 1532 ... without a fight'; on 8 February 1533 Min Bin 'received tributes from local lords of Bengal'.
March 1533: the Ahoms win the naval battle of Duimunisila ('The invading forces lost 2,500 men, 20 ships'); Turbak was killed near the Bharali River and the Ahoms pursued to the Karatoya.
13 April 1533: 'He left Dhaka for Mrauk-U on 13 April 1533'; 'his control of Bengal beyond Chittagong, where coins bearing his name and styling him sultan were struck, was nominal'.
March 1534: Sher Shah beats Mahmud's forces at Surajgarh ('winning a decisive victory'; Ibrahim Khan killed).

1536-1537: 'Sher Shah repeatedly defeated Mahmud and took all lands west of the Teliagarhi pass'; the sultan 'held the Teliagarhi pass (1536 AD)', then paid over 13,000,000 gold coins and ceded territory up to Sakrigali.
6 April 1538: Mahmud 'finally decisively defeated by Sher Shah Suri on 6 April 1538'; Gaur sacked.
6 April 1538: the Hussain Shahi sultanate falls.

wars.name: Ilyas Shah's Nepal raid
wars.outcome: Ilyas Shah's army 'looted Kathmandu city for three days' and sacked Swayambhunath, then returned to Bengal 'with plentiful spoils'; a raid, no hold, so no occupation event is recorded (repair 2026-10-20; the Kathmandu dossier has none).

wars.name: Delhi-Bengal war (Ekdala sieges)
wars.outcome: 1353: Firuz Shah Tughluq occupied Pandua and besieged Ilyas at Ekdala; Bengal agreed to pay tribute and lost unnamed conquests; he withdrew in 1355.

wars.name: Bengal-Jaunpur War
wars.outcome: 'Parts of Jaunpur were annexed' (Bengal page, no place named; read as Tirhut north of the Ganga).

wars.name: Bengal and the Arakan wars
wars.outcome: 1429-1430 Bengali forces back Min Saw Mon and Arakan becomes a vassal; 1459 Arakan defeats Barbak Shah and takes Chittagong; 1512-1516 Hussain Shah restores Bengali sovereignty over Chittagong and northern Arakan.

wars.name: Bengal-Gajapati war of 1447-1450
wars.outcome: Kapilendra Deva's army took territory west of the Ganga including Gar Mandaran (Gopinathpur inscription 1447; Puri inscription 1450 'the conquest of Gauda'); no page dates a Gajapati loss of it, and Mandaran is Bengal's in 1508.

wars.name: Bengal-Kamata War
wars.outcome: Muzaffar Shah's 898 AH conquest of 1492-93; the Khen dynasty overthrown in 1498; Ismail Ghazi imprisoned King Nilambar and annexed the land up to Hajo in 1499.

wars.name: Lodi invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: Sikandar Lodi invaded in 1496; the armies met at Barh and a treaty gave the country west of Barh to Lodi and left the country east of Barh with Husain Shah.

wars.name: Bengal-Gajapati border wars
wars.outcome: Ismail Ghazi's raid reached Puri in 1508-1509 and was driven back; by 1515 Orissa was a Bengal vassal.

wars.name: Battle of Ghaghra
wars.outcome: 6 May 1529: the Mughals beat the Afghans and Bengalis but did not enter Bengal; Nasrat Shah sued for peace and kept independence.

wars.name: Gauda-Ahom War
wars.outcome: Turbak's invasion was destroyed at Duimunisila in March 1533 and he was killed near the Bharali River; no border moved.

wars.name: Arakanese invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: 7 October 1532 Min Bin's invasion beats a Bengal army and takes Chittagong; Dhaka entered 11 December 1532 and left 13 April 1533; control beyond Chittagong nominal.

wars.name: Sher Shah Suri's conquest of Bengal
wars.outcome: Surajgarh in March 1534; the Teliagarhi pass held in 1536; the lands west of it lost in 1536-37 with a huge indemnity; Gaur sacked on 6 April 1538.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the Delhi, Jaunpur and Arakan frontiers are approximate.

The Barh treaty of 1496 is the one dated frontier on the pages ('the country west of Barh went to Sikandar Lodi'), but it is given in words, not as a line, and the page's own inscriptions (Hussainabad of Balia district 1501-1502, 'firm…
